market_holds: Spot 152.98 at the 18:08 UTC seal (Yahoo; 15-minute bars show ~155 at 14:30 ET). Options: front-expiry (11/20) straddle 16.7%, event-implied move 14.5%, 25d skew +4.1 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.45, ATM spread 35% of mid so indicative only (sealed baseline). Median of the last 7 close-to-close reactions is 8.0%, 5 of 7 down; but at the scored open the Q3 FY26 reaction was larger than close-to-close: 219.72 close to a 191.71 open (-12.7%), then -3.8% by the close. The stock is 52.5% below its 52w high (328, May 2026, post 3:1 split), -7.7% over 20 sessions after the post-midterm data-center selloff (Nov 4-5: 163.34 -> 125.06), and has rebounded to ~154. Today it rose ~+8% while every peer fell (VRT -6.7%, GEV -4.5%, ETN -4.2%, NVT -4.6%, HUBB -2.8%, IESC -2.3%, SPY -1.9%), almost all of it in the first 30 minutes on heavy volume, and I found no news, filing or analyst note to explain it. That is about 12 points of relative run-in on the print day. Consensus for Q4 FY26 (Sep quarter): revenue $341.8M (FXEmpire, 5 analysts) to $330.8M (Benzinga), EPS $1.54-1.58; Sidoti cut Q4 EPS from 1.78 to 1.59 after Q3. Against Q4 FY25's $298.0M and $1.41 split-adjusted, that is +11% to +15% revenue growth. No formal guide. On the Q3 call the CFO said growth would not be double digit y/y given the backlog conversion rate. Backlog was $2.4B at Jun 30, with 54% ($1.3B) expected within 12 months. Short interest is about 2.9M shares, 4 days to cover (Equibles, as of Nov 13). Consensus PT $187.92; JPMorgan cut to $250 OW on Oct 13; Cantor Neutral $235.
view: There are two lines here. One is the headline: the revenue and EPS consensus look stale against management's own steer. FY26 revenue growth went +4%, +6%, +9% by quarter. Q3 missed revenue ($311.7M vs $321.5M) and EPS ($1.42 vs $1.49). The CFO then told the Street that y/y growth would not reach double digits, yet the Q4 consensus still implies +11-15% ($331-342M). Rebuilding the quarter at about +9% y/y gives roughly $325M, and with SG&A pressure from the facility ramp, EPS lands around $1.45-1.52 against $1.55-1.58. So a headline miss is more likely than not. At the open, that headline counted for a lot last time: Q3 opened -12.7% on a miss despite record orders. The other line, which has driven three of the last four reactions, is orders, backlog and the outlook: Q4 FY25 fell -11% on soft orders, Q1 FY26 rose +16% and Q2 FY26 +9% on big orders. Q4 orders will fall sequentially from Q3's $934M record, which included the $400M+ data-center order. I cannot see whether a new mega order (an LNG package after the May-June Commonwealth and Delfin FIDs, or data-center phase 2) landed in the quarter. Management will also be asked about the political and Texas permitting risk to data-center capex. Against the headline-miss lean: the stock has already halved from its high, sentiment is washed out, and someone bid it ~12% relative to peers today for no visible reason, which could be short covering or informed positioning. Net: a modest lean down, mostly from the stale revenue bar, too uncertain on orders to bet.
unpriced: The Q4 revenue consensus (+11-15% y/y) has not absorbed the CFO's August statement that growth would not be double digit given backlog conversion. This is a stale-estimate bias that already showed in the Q3 revenue miss. The options price a large move but not a direction from this, and today's +8% against falling peers raises the bar further. It is only a lean, because orders, which I cannot observe, have usually decided the reaction.

recommendation.reason: Consensus Q4 revenue of $331-342M implies +11-15% y/y, against the CFO's on-record steer of below double digits and a +4/+6/+9% trajectory. A headline revenue/EPS miss is therefore likely, and the last miss gapped the stock -12.7% at the open. But orders and backlog have decided three of the last four reactions, I cannot see Q4 orders, and today's unexplained +8% against a falling sector may be informed. So the edge does not reach the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A large new order in the quarter (an LNG mega package or a data-center phase 2), with book-to-bill above about 1.3 and confident FY27 commentary that the data-center pipeline is intact. That would override a revenue miss, as it did in Q2.

self_critique: The Street knows the CFO's comment and Q3's miss, so buy-side whisper numbers may already sit below the $342M published figure. Two of the five estimates may be stale, and the effective bar may be closer to $330M, which a +10% quarter would meet. Orders and outlook have decided most reactions, and Q4 could carry an LNG mega award. After a 52% drawdown and a crowded-out sector, a relief rally on 'no cancellations, pipeline intact' is plausible. Today's idiosyncratic bid hints that someone expects good news.
approach_notes: P4 (stale estimates against management's own words) found the one concrete gap quickly, and P6 (find the line it trades on) correctly showed that orders, not the headline, usually decide this name, which kept me from overcommitting. Comparing peer tapes for the same day surfaced the unexplained relative bid, which the playbook does not prompt for but was informative.
